To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sensitivity and specificity of MRI in detecting marrow infiltration in patients with lymphoid malignancies are 90% and 94%, respectively, and that MRI is the best imaging method for the detection of bone marrow lesions in patients with lymphoproliferative diseases.

bone marrow imaging is a promising technique to improve the detection of bone marrow disease and to guide biopsy in lymphoma, and that the use of multimodality imaging, including PET/CT, is the most promising future strategy.

(1) MRI is currently the best imaging modality for the assessment of bone marrow involvement by lymphoma; (2) PET/CT and SPECT/CT are the most promising modalities for guiding BMB in lymphoma; (3) PET/MRI may be the most promising future modality for the imaging of bone marrow involvement.
